title: Important Differences: DPSP vs Fundamental Rights

blocks.content: Fundamental Rights aim at establishing political democracy, while Directive Principles aim at establishing social and economic democracy.

rows: Establish Social and Economic Welfare State

items: Justiciability Difference: FRs are directly enforceable in courts under Article 32 (Supreme Court) and Article 226 (High Court), whereas DPSPs are non-justiciable.
Landmark Cases: Champakam Dorairajan (1951) held that FRs prevail over DPSPs; Minerva Mills (1980) restored balance between Part III and Part IV.
Article 31C Exception: Laws enacted to implement Article 39(b) and 39(c) cannot be declared void on the ground of violating Article 14 or Article 19.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Rights (Part III) protect individual liberties and seek to establish political democracy in India.
Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) act as guidelines for the State to establish a social and economic welfare state.
Fundamental Rights act as negative obligations (limitations on State power), whereas DPSPs are positive obligations (actions the State should take).
Fundamental Rights carry legal sanctions and are directly enforceable, while DPSPs carry moral and political sanctions.
In the Minerva Mills case (1980), the Supreme Court emphasized that the Constitution is founded on the bedrock of the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
